trials.notes: Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), next_tag('H1'), a depth-bounded next_token() walk, get_token_type() === '#text', and get_modifiable_text() for decoded text. All called methods are documented in the rendered files and execution reported no _doing_it_wrong records. Small penalty: the final get_last_error()/paused_at_incomplete_token() guard is conservative for a read-only extraction contract that says null means no H1; docs allow caller policy here, but this could wrongly collapse some truncated-input cases into null.

Correct processor choice and fully documented API usage. The single next_token() state machine is idiomatic for structural text extraction: it detects the first H1 opener, tracks its recorded depth, appends only #text token get_modifiable_text(), and returns an empty string for an empty heading. No misuse records.

Essentially matches the canonical documented pattern: fragment HTML Processor, next_tag('H1'), record current depth, walk tokens while depth stays within the subtree, append decoded #text via get_modifiable_text(). All methods are documented and all edge cases in the hidden set passed.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all hidden cases, so there are no failed hidden cases to attribute to a documentation gap. The docs worked well because html-processor.md explicitly says to choose WP_HTML_Processor for structure-aware text extraction, provides a 'collect DOM-style text from a subtree' recipe, explains that get_modifiable_text() on #text returns decoded text, and emphasizes the >= depth boundary needed to survive nested closers and virtual closers from unclosed elements. The main near-miss is Trial 1's stated policy of returning null on incomplete input: it did not fail the hidden unclosed-H1 case, because unclosed elements are tokenized with virtual closers and do not set paused_at_incomplete_token(), but it shows some risk of cargo-culting mutation-style completeness checks into read-only extraction contracts.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs describe incomplete syntax and virtual closing behavior, but the distinction between an unclosed element and a truly incomplete trailing token can still be easy to blur.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short cross-reference example contrasting an unclosed element that still produces structural closers with a mid-token truncation that sets paused_at_incomplete_token() only after the cursor reaches it.

doc_gaps.problem: The mutation recipe prominently shows fail-closed checks, while the read-only extraction policy is mostly prose. Trial 1 copied the checks into a read-only helper whose null return had a narrower meaning.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an explicit note: for read-only extraction, only reject paused_at_incomplete_token() or get_last_error() when the caller contract requires complete input; do not reuse a not-found sentinel for truncation unless that is part of the contract.

doc_gaps.problem: The method docs identify unsupported-parser aborts, but could better explain how this interacts with data already accumulated during a read-only walk.
doc_gaps.suggestion: State that get_last_error() does not invalidate tokens already visited; callers should choose and document whether to return partial data, a separate error sentinel, or a fallback when unsupported markup stops the scan.
